recoveryRoadmap.description: Step-by-step survival and recovery plan for dependent family members when the primary earner is incapacitated or deceased. Follow phases in order — do not skip ahead.

phases.title: Immediate Survival
phases.focus: Access liquid cash, stop auto-debits, obtain death certificates, notify institutions

keyActions.action: Obtain Death Certificate — apply at Municipal Corporation/Gram Panchayat within 21 days. Get minimum 15 certified copies.
keyActions.why: Every single claim, bank, and legal process requires a certified copy. Running out means delays of weeks.

keyActions.action: Access liquid cash immediately — joint 'Either or Survivor' accounts need NO court order. Withdraw what you need before notifying the bank to freeze.
keyActions.why: Joint account survivors have full legal rights. Notifying bank too early freezes your access unnecessarily.

keyActions.action: List ALL auto-debits, SIPs, EMIs and standing instructions — pause or cancel them BEFORE they bounce and attract penalties.
keyActions.why: Bounced EMIs after death notification damage credit history and attract charges on an already-stressed account.

keyActions.action: Notify the deceased's employer within 2-3 days to initiate: salary arrears, gratuity (Form F), group life insurance, and EDLI claims.
keyActions.why: Employers hold group term policies worth 3-5x salary. Gratuity must be paid within 30 days of becoming payable.

keyActions.action: Intimate ALL insurance companies (LIC + private) about the death. Early intimation is required — IRDAI mandates 30-day settlement from document submission.
keyActions.why: Claims filed within first 3 years of policy issuance may be investigated. Early intimation starts the clock on your side.

keyActions.action: Apply for Legal Heir Certificate from the Tehsildar/Revenue Authority. Takes 15-30 days and unlocks most claims without a court order.
keyActions.why: Faster and cheaper than a Succession Certificate. Accepted by most banks, employers, and insurance companies.

keyActions.action: Secure ALL original documents: property papers, insurance policy bonds, FD receipts, Aadhaar, PAN, will. Check bank locker, home safe, and email for e-policies.
keyActions.why: Original policy bond is required by LIC. Lost originals delay claims by months.

mustHaveDocuments: Death Certificate — 15 certified copies minimum
Cremation / Burial Certificate (needed to get death certificate)
Aadhaar + PAN of deceased and all claimants
Marriage Certificate (for spouse claims)
Birth Certificates of children
Passport-size photographs — 10 each for all claimants
Bank passbooks and last 3 months statements
Last 3 salary slips of deceased (from employer)
Original insurance policy bonds
Ration Card / Family ID card

keyContacts.use: Policy status and death claim intimation
If insurer delays or rejects claim

criticalMistakes: Getting fewer than 10 death certificate copies — you will need 15+ across all claims
Notifying the bank about death BEFORE withdrawing from a joint 'Either or Survivor' account — survivor has full rights, no permission needed
Paying off the deceased's personal loans immediately without first checking if a credit life insurance policy exists on the loan
Discarding original insurance policy bonds thinking digital is sufficient — LIC and many insurers still require originals
Sharing OTPs or account credentials with agents or touts who offer to 'expedite' claims — this is fraud
Not looking for a Will — check email, bank locker, and lawyer's office before assuming intestate succession

legalDeadlines.consequence: After 30 days, a Magistrate's order is required — adds weeks
Claims beyond 3 years may be time-barred under the Limitation Act, 1963

legalDeadlines.deadline: 30 days from when it becomes payable
legalDeadlines.consequence: Employer must pay interest on delay under Section 7(3A), Payment of Gratuity Act

jointAccountRules.either_or_survivor: Surviving holder has immediate full access. Bank only needs death certificate to remove deceased's name. No court order needed.
jointAccountRules.former_or_survivor: If deceased was 'Former' holder — survivor accesses on submitting death certificate. No delay.
jointAccountRules.single_holder_account: Account is frozen on death intimation. Nominee claims with death certificate + ID. Without nominee: Legal Heir Certificate or Succession Certificate required. RBI allows simplified claims up to ₹5 lakh.

phases.title: Claim & Transfer
phases.focus: File all insurance and EPF claims, initiate bank and demat transmission, begin succession process

keyActions.action: File LIC/insurance death claim: submit claimant's statement, original policy bond, death certificate, NEFT bank details. Track the 30-day IRDAI settlement clock.
keyActions.why: IRDAI mandates settlement within 30 days of full document submission. Insurer must pay 2% above bank rate for every day of delay beyond this.

keyActions.action: File THREE EPF claims together via employer or EPFO office: Form 20 (PF withdrawal) + Form 10D (monthly pension) + Form 5IF (EDLI insurance up to ₹7 lakh). Most families miss EDLI entirely.
keyActions.why: EDLI is a free life insurance benefit that pays up to ₹7 lakh. It is a separate claim from PF and pension — all three must be filed independently.

keyActions.action: Initiate bank account transmission for single-holder accounts: submit Transmission Request, death certificate, Legal Heir Certificate, and indemnity bond at the branch.
keyActions.why: With nominee: simple KYC + death certificate. Without nominee and amount >₹5 lakh: Succession Certificate from Civil Court is required.

keyActions.action: Close PPF account by submitting Form C at the bank or post office where the account is held. Nominee/legal heir receives full balance + accrued interest.
keyActions.why: PPF can be closed prematurely on death — the 15-year lock-in does not apply. Interest is credited until closure.

keyActions.action: File Demat account transmission with the Depository Participant (DP): submit Transmission Request Form + death certificate + nominee/heir KYC.
keyActions.why: Without nominee and value >₹5 lakh (SEBI threshold): Succession Certificate required. With nominee: straightforward in 2-3 weeks.

keyActions.action: Claim mutual fund units through CAMS or KFintech (not just the broker). If held in folio mode, approach each AMC directly with death certificate and KYC.
keyActions.why: Broker platforms may not cover all folios. CAMS and KFintech hold the actual records. Missing folios = lost money.

keyActions.action: Apply for Succession Certificate from District Civil Court under Section 372, Indian Succession Act, if assets exceed bank/SEBI thresholds and no nominee exists.
keyActions.why: Takes 3-6 months. File early. Required for large bank balances, securities, and debentures without a nominee.

Claimant's Statement in insurer's prescribed form

Legal Heir Certificate
Cancelled cheque of claimant (NEFT details)

KYC of all claimants — Aadhaar + PAN
Form 20 (EPF) + Form 10D (Pension) + Form 5IF (EDLI)
Employer's certificate confirming death, date of joining, and last salary
Succession Certificate (if amounts exceed threshold and no nominee)
criticalMistakes: Filing only EPF withdrawal (Form 20) and missing EDLI insurance (Form 5IF) — this is a free ₹7 lakh benefit that most families never claim
Assuming the bank will automatically transfer FDs to nominee — each fixed deposit must be individually claimed or transmitted
Not filing insurance claim because original policy bond is lost — insurers cannot deny a valid claim for a missing bond; file for duplicate first
Not checking employer email and SMS history for group or term insurance policies the deceased may have enrolled in
Signing blank indemnity bonds or NOC papers without reading — get a lawyer to review before signing

legalDeadlines.deadline: 30 days from receipt of all documents
legalDeadlines.consequence: Insurer must pay penalty interest. File complaint on IRDAI IGMS portal if delayed.
File grievance at EPFiGMS portal: https://epfigms.gov.in

legalDeadlines.consequence: Employer pays interest under Section 7(3A) of Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972

phases.title: Legal & Financial Settlement
phases.focus: Property mutation, will probate, final income tax filing, loan insurance claims, utility transfers

keyActions.action: File the deceased's final Income Tax Return as Legal Representative under Section 159, Income Tax Act. Register as 'Legal Representative' on the income tax portal first.
keyActions.why: Legal representative is personally liable for unpaid taxes. Missing this return attracts penalties under Section 234A/B/C.

keyActions.action: Initiate property mutation (revenue record name change) at Talathi/Tehsildar/Municipal Corporation. This is NOT a title transfer — it updates government records only.
keyActions.why: Property tax continues to accrue in deceased's name until mutation. Mutation is required before any future sale or mortgage.

keyActions.action: Check ALL loans (home, car, personal) for credit life insurance before paying a single EMI. Home loans especially — most have mandatory insurance. File the claim with the lender's insurance partner.
keyActions.why: Paying EMIs when a credit life policy exists means paying out of pocket for a liability that is already insured. Stop payments until insurance status is confirmed.

keyActions.action: File for Probate of Will at District Court or High Court. Mandatory in Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai. Strongly recommended elsewhere for clean property transfers.
keyActions.why: Without probate, property buyers and banks will question title validity. Probate establishes Will as legally operative.

keyActions.action: Transfer all utility connections (electricity, gas, water, phone, broadband) to surviving member's name using death certificate and ID proof.
keyActions.why: Utilities in deceased's name cannot be modified or ported. Disconnection risk if ownership is disputed.

keyActions.action: Transfer vehicle RC to legal heir at RTO using Form 31. Simultaneously transfer motor insurance — vehicle cannot be insured without RC in living person's name.
keyActions.why: Driving or selling a vehicle with RC in deceased's name creates legal and insurance complications.

mustHaveDocuments: Registered Will (original) OR Probate Order from court
Succession Certificate (for movable assets without nominee)
Property title deeds — original Sale Deed and Mother Deed chain
Encumbrance Certificate (EC) from Sub-Registrar — 13 years minimum
Latest property tax receipt
Khata Certificate or Patta (state-specific revenue document)
Income Tax Returns of deceased — last 3 years
Form 26AS and Form 16 of deceased for the final year
Loan sanction letters and outstanding principal statements
Credit life insurance policy documents (ask lender if unsure)

keyContacts.use: Register as Legal Representative and file deceased's return
Verify if any hidden mortgage or charge exists on property

criticalMistakes: Confusing property MUTATION with ownership TRANSFER — mutation updates revenue records only; ownership transfer requires a registered deed
Not filing the deceased's income tax return — the legal representative is personally liable for unpaid tax and penalties
Paying home loan EMIs without confirming whether a credit life insurance policy settles the loan on death
Attempting to sell property before completing mutation and obtaining succession/probate — buyers and banks will refuse
Not obtaining an Encumbrance Certificate before transfer — hidden mortgages will surface later and invalidate sale
Ignoring daughters' rights — post-2005 amendment to Hindu Succession Act gives daughters equal coparcenary rights in ancestral property

legalDeadlines.deadline: July 31 of the assessment year following the year of death
legalDeadlines.consequence: Penalty up to ₹10,000 under Section 234F + interest under 234A/B/C

legalDeadlines.deadline: No statutory deadline, but file within 3 years (Limitation Act)
legalDeadlines.consequence: Delay increases risk of dispute; adverse possession risk after 12 years

legalDeadlines.deadline: No hard deadline, but complete before any sale or loan
legalDeadlines.consequence: Property tax accrues in deceased's name; future transactions are blocked

minorChildrenRights.inheritance: Minor children are Class I legal heirs under Hindu Succession Act and inherit equally with spouse
minorChildrenRights.guardian: Mother is the natural guardian — no court appointment needed
minorChildrenRights.restriction: Natural guardian CANNOT sell, mortgage, or gift the minor's immovable property without court permission (Section 8, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956)
minorChildrenRights.account: Minor's inherited share should be held in a separate bank account in the minor's name, operated by mother as guardian
minorChildrenRights.majority: On turning 18, the child has full independent rights over inherited assets

phases.title: Restructure & Rebuild
phases.focus: Protect the family you have left, prevent this from happening to your heirs, rebuild financial stability

keyActions.action: Update nominations on EVERY financial account immediately — bank accounts, FDs, demat, mutual funds, PPF, NPS, and all insurance policies. Do not leave a single account without a nominee.
keyActions.why: The entire pain of this process was caused by missing nominations. This one action prevents your family from going through the same ordeal.

keyActions.action: Draft a Will and register it at the Sub-Registrar's office. Registration costs ₹500-1000 in most states. An unregistered Will is valid but easier to challenge.
keyActions.why: You have just experienced what happens without a Will. A registered Will eliminates ambiguity and speeds up property transfer to months, not years.

keyActions.action: Purchase adequate term life insurance for all earning members — minimum coverage should be 10x annual household expenses. Buy immediately before any existing policy lapses.
keyActions.why: Health insurance portability and continuity benefits are lost after a break. Lock in health coverage before the transition period disrupts existing policies.

keyActions.action: Build a liquid emergency fund covering 6-12 months of household expenses in a savings account or liquid mutual fund. This is priority over any investment.
keyActions.why: The first 30 days of a crisis are survivable only with accessible liquid cash. Locked-in FDs, PPF, and equity do not help in an emergency.

keyActions.action: Create a written Asset Register documenting: all account numbers, nominees, access credentials, document locations, and advisor contacts. Store one copy in bank locker and share with one trusted person.
keyActions.why: This document IS the emergency kit. You now know the value of having it — create it for your family before they need it.

keyActions.action: Consolidate scattered bank accounts, demat accounts, and MF folios to reduce the number of institutions your heirs will need to deal with.
keyActions.why: Every account you hold is a claim your heirs must file. Fewer accounts = significantly less paperwork and fewer chances for assets to be forgotten.

keyActions.action: Execute a registered Power of Attorney for a trusted family member to manage your financial affairs if you are incapacitated.
keyActions.why: Critical if you are now a single parent. A registered POA allows action on your behalf without court delays.

mustHaveDocuments: Registered Will (latest version)
Updated nomination forms for all accounts (filed and acknowledged)
Registered Power of Attorney
New term life insurance policy documents
New or renewed health insurance policy
Asset Register (physical + digital encrypted copy)
Children's investment and education fund documents
Updated KYC across all institutions

keyContacts.use: Complaints against mutual funds, brokers, demat
NPS account queries and nominee update
Find a SEBI-registered or CFP-certified advisor for restructuring

criticalMistakes: Not updating nominations — the single most common mistake that forces the next generation to go through this same process
Investing an inherited lump sum immediately and aggressively — grief impairs financial judgment; park it in a liquid fund for 3-6 months first
Letting health insurance lapse during the transition — you lose continuity benefits and waiting period exemptions permanently
Keeping all assets in one person's name again — distribute, use joint holdings, and ensure each account has a nominee
Not making a Will because 'I'm young' — this crisis is the proof that financial planning has no age requirement
Ignoring tax on inherited assets — inheritance is not taxed in India, but capital gains on subsequent sale of inherited assets ARE taxable

legalDeadlines.deadline: Before policy expiry (30-day grace period typical)
legalDeadlines.consequence: Loss of no-claim bonus, continuity, and waiting period benefits. Fresh waiting periods imposed.

legalDeadlines.deadline: No deadline — do it this week
legalDeadlines.consequence: Without a nominee, your family faces the same months-long process you just survived
Unregistered Will is valid but can be contested. Registered Will is harder to challenge.
